prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: The first-round exchange did not change my scientific judgment. The GLP-1 chain is complete and independently replicated: proglucagon processing, identification of the truncated active peptide and its insulinotropic physiology (Holst), receptor biology and the intestinotrophic and cardiometabolic actions (Drucker), and the chemistry and synthesis of the active form (Mojsov). Randomized outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease show that the biology was correct. No member argues for waiting, and I agree, because delay adds no evidence. Unanimity at the opening is not my reason. The reason is that this is the one shortlisted achievement where mechanism, replication and patient benefit are all established, and a discovery-based citation fits in three names. I keep the single-part prize with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the main weakness. Mojsov's weight relative to Habener, who is outside the credited names, is disputed, and the file cannot settle it. Several of us, me included, are working from unverified recollection. A discovery-only citation also leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues reached patients, so some readers will see a prize for the hormone and not the drug. I still think that is a legitimate cost, because the citation can be written to honour the discovery and its enabling role without claiming the drug programme. If the committee judged Mojsov's contribution too uncertain to credit, I would prefer Knudsen in her place to a configuration that names no third person, and I would not block it.

responses.point: Linnarsson prefers Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, saying the acylation-based design behind liraglutide and semaglutide is an original contribution, and that I would drop the person whose work most directly produced the therapy for a credit I cannot verify.
responses.response: That is a fair challenge, and I agree that acylation for protracted action was design work and not a routine optimisation. I still keep Mojsov, for two reasons. First, the verification problem applies to both choices. The Habener question is open, but Knudsen's contribution is documented, so I would be judging a documented contribution against a disputed one, and it does not follow that the disputed one is the weaker discovery. Second, Knudsen's work is the translation of a mechanism that others had already identified, and a citation that stays on discovery lets the prize rest on what is scientifically new. I answer your question directly: I would accept your trio if the Mojsov question stays unresolved, but I would write the citation to state the discovery and the enabled therapy, not to credit the analogue programme.

responses.point: Sandberg says dropping the person whose work gave patients a long-acting drug leaves the therapeutic half of the citation without a named contributor, and that she could move to a Mojsov trio if the citation were narrowed to physiology and peptide identification.
responses.response: Your offer is workable, and I would meet it. A citation that says 'for discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment' makes the claim narrowly: it credits the discovery and states what it made possible, without crediting the design of any drug. That is accurate for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and the therapeutic outcome appears as consequence, not as a named contribution. I do not think the therapeutic half is left unattributed, because the citation names the discovery on which the therapies depend. I agree that the prize has rewarded industrial development sparingly, and that is the main reason I do not widen the credit to the analogue programme.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would not object strongly to a Knudsen variant if Mojsov's priority proved too uncertain, and she ranks CAR-T (B021) ahead of the unfolded protein response as the first alternative.
responses.response: We agree on the primary configuration, and your fallback matches mine. On the alternatives I still put B006 ahead of B021. Mori and Walter have a clean two-name credit with no priority dispute and three decades of confirmation. CAR-T is clinically more transformative, but Eshhar and first-generation CAR work are outside the credited names, and neither a two- nor a three-person credit closes that gap. I accept your point that the disease link for the unfolded protein response is indirect. For a prize meant to reward discovery, I weigh originality and clean attribution above breadth of clinical use. I would not choose B021 ahead of B006 this year, but I do not rule it out for a later one.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps the Mojsov trio and says the three-person set recognises the discovery of the active form and action of the hormone, which is what the prize can credit most cleanly.
responses.response: I share your reading and your reservation. Your point that unanimous opening support reflects a well-known story, not verified history, is one I accept, and it is why I keep recording that my recollection of Habener and Mojsov is unverified. We differ only in how firmly to hold the line against Knudsen: I am prepared to accept the Knudsen trio, while your position seems to treat the discovery trio as the only clean one. My view is that two defensible third names make the choice a matter of what the citation honours, and not a question of one being wrong.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority relative to Habener cannot be settled from the supplied evidence, and my account of that history is from memory.
Whether the committee wants a discovery-only citation or one that credits drug design. I prefer the former, and I would accept the Knudsen variant for the third name.

A two-part prize (B005 with B006) would require removing a B005 laureate under the three-person cap. I would not accept that cost, because it weakens the better-supported achievement to add a second part.
Whether B006 or B021 is the stronger alternative this year. I rank B006 first but the difference is not large.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I use optogenetics (B042) as a method in circuit work, with no documented tie to its credited names, and B042 is not in my configuration. My documented collaborations (Grillner, Ernfors, Perlmann, including a 2009 paper with Perlmann) involve no shortlisted candidate. Perlmann's round-1 position is close to mine, and I note the co-authorship for transparency. I do not request recusal for anyone.
